title: Drive the robot to the charger
instruction: Build a program from moves and turns. The robot carries it out literally.
debrief: The robot doesn't work anything out for itself. Every step must be unambiguous and the order exact. More than one correct algorithm leads to the goal, and repeating makes the program shorter.

levels.instruction: The robot faces up. The charger is 2 squares up and 3 to the right.
levels.why: Up 2, turn right, right 3. Or the other way round: first right, then up. Both algorithms are correct.

levels.instruction: The way up is blocked. Try another way.
levels.why: When one way is closed, the other algorithm helps: first right, then up.

levels.instruction: A longer way, but the program may have only 6 commands. Use repeat.
levels.why: 4× forward, turn right, 4× forward: five commands instead of nine. Repeating makes the program shorter.
